articles.title: Blocking vs Non-blocking Assignments
articles.summary: Understand procedural assignment timing and why sequential logic typically uses non-blocking assignments.
articles.code: always_ff @(posedge clk) begin\n  q <= d; // update after the time step\nend
articles.takeaway: Use blocking assignments for many combinational procedural calculations and non-blocking assignments for clocked state updates, following the coding style required by your project.

articles.title: Latch Inference and How to Avoid It
articles.summary: Learn why incomplete combinational assignments can infer storage unintentionally.
articles.takeaway: Assign every output on every path in combinational logic.

articles.title: FIFO Full and Empty Logic
articles.summary: Explore pointer relationships and status-flag reasoning in FIFO designs.
articles.code: // Example only: exact logic depends on FIFO architecture\nempty = (wr_ptr == rd_ptr);
articles.takeaway: Pointer wrap, extra pointer bits, and memory depth determine the correct full/empty equations.

articles.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Reset
articles.summary: Compare reset behavior relative to the active clock edge.
articles.takeaway: Choose reset strategy based on the design specification and reset-domain requirements.

articles.title: Moore vs Mealy State Machines
articles.summary: Compare outputs that depend on state alone with outputs that also depend on inputs.
articles.code: // Moore: output is a function of current state\nassign out = (state == ACTIVE);
articles.takeaway: Choose the FSM style based on timing, latency, and output-glitch requirements.

articles.title: Assertions and Functional Coverage
articles.summary: Use properties to catch temporal failures and coverage to measure exercised scenarios.
articles.takeaway: Assertions check behavior; coverage helps identify scenarios your tests have not exercised.
